`shipkeep` is a single static binary for Linux, macOS and Windows, on amd64 and arm64. Each [release](https://github.com/shipkeepdev/shipkeep/releases) attaches it as `shipkeep_<version>_<os>_<arch>`. It talks to the control plane's API with an API token.

- The token is read from a prompt or from standard input, never from a flag: a flag would land in the shell history and the process list.
- `login` saves the address and the token in a file only you can read. `SHIPKEEP_URL` and `SHIPKEEP_TOKEN` replace the saved login, for automation.
- Commands that reach an environment take `--org`, `--project` and `--env`, or `SHIPKEEP_ORG`, `SHIPKEEP_PROJECT` and `SHIPKEEP_ENV`. Each is an identifier, which the environment's address in the web UI shows: `/orgs/<organization>/projects/<project>/environments/<environment>`.
- A flag takes one or two dashes. A misplaced flag or an extra argument is refused, never ignored.
- The exit status is 0 on success, 1 when the command failed, and 2 when it was not understood.

## `shipkeep login`

Save a control plane address and an API token.

```text
shipkeep login [flags]

  --url string
      control plane URL, https://...
```

## `shipkeep logout`

Forget the saved address and token on this machine. It takes no flag.

```text
shipkeep logout
```

## `shipkeep init`

Write a shipkeep.yml.

```text
shipkeep init [flags]

  --file string
      file to write (default "shipkeep.yml")
  --force
      replace an existing file
  --image string
      container image
  --name string
      application name
  --port int
      port the application listens on (default 80)
```

## `shipkeep status`

Show applications, their latest deployment and replicas.

```text
shipkeep status [flags]

  --app string
      show only this application
  --env string
      environment ID
  --org string
      organization ID
  --project string
      project ID
```

## `shipkeep secrets list`

Show the names of an environment's secrets.

```text
shipkeep secrets list [flags]

  --env string
      environment ID
  --org string
      organization ID
  --project string
      project ID
```

## `shipkeep secrets set`

Set a secret, reading its value from standard input.

```text
shipkeep secrets set NAME [flags]

  --env string
      environment ID
  --org string
      organization ID
  --project string
      project ID
```

## `shipkeep secrets unset`

Remove a secret.

```text
shipkeep secrets unset NAME [flags]

  --env string
      environment ID
  --org string
      organization ID
  --project string
      project ID
```

## `shipkeep deploy`

Save shipkeep.yml on the control plane and deploy it.

```text
shipkeep deploy [flags]

  --env string
      environment ID
  --file string
      configuration file (default "shipkeep.yml")
  --no-wait
      return once the deployment is queued
  --org string
      organization ID
  --project string
      project ID
  --timeout duration
      how long to follow the deployment (default 15m0s)
```

## `shipkeep rollback`

Return to an earlier good release.

```text
shipkeep rollback [flags]

  --app string
      application name, instead of reading the file
  --env string
      environment ID
  --file string
      configuration file naming the application (default "shipkeep.yml")
  --no-wait
      return once the deployment is queued
  --org string
      organization ID
  --project string
      project ID
  --timeout duration
      how long to follow the deployment (default 15m0s)
  --to string
      deployment to return to; by default the last good one before the current release
```

## `shipkeep server remove`

Remove a server, given its exact name with --confirm.

```text
shipkeep server remove SERVER_ID [flags]

  --confirm string
      the server's exact name; removal cannot be undone
  --org string
      organization ID
```
